subject: Key eviction & encrypted snapshot procedure for private deployments (KEP-SP)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Key eviction & encrypted snapshot procedure for private deployments (KEP-SP)

Team —

After the on-call incident last month and a follow-up review with platform, I sketched a compact runbook for handling operator compromise or host-snapshot events in Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). This is focused on customer-managed KMS/HSM BYOK flows where we need deterministic, low-impact remediation for keys and secrets while preserving recoverability for customers.

High level goals:
- Provide an auditable, reversible snapshot strategy for keystores so customers can recover from legitimate restores without re-seeding secrets.
- Rapidly evict operator credentials or compromised wrapping keys without breaking customer workload availability where possible.
- Minimize blast radius by using ephemeral wrapping keys + delegation ACLs and well-scoped attestations.

Summary of proposed KEP-SP steps (short):
1) Detection & Triage: Confirm compromise triggers (host snapshot restore, operator key exfil, unauthorized HSM access). Log current unseal tokens, active operator sessions, and the KV-access ledger (t0 snapshot).
2) Freeze & Snapshot: Create an encrypted snapshot of the keystore (sealed with a short-lived asymmetric key protected by a remote KMS) and a separate integrity manifest. Store snapshot off-cluster in customer-approved storage (S3-compatible with bucket-level SSE-KMS).
3) Eviction flow: Rotate the wrapping key (stepwise): generate new tenant wrapping key pair, rewrap symmetric KEKs for active keys, mark old wrapping key as revoked in KMS and publish audit event. Suspend operator-of-record access until re-attestation.
4) Gradual rebind: For critical services, enable a temporary dual-wrapped mode where tokens accept both old and new KEKs for a short T-window (e.g., 10 minutes) to limit outages; then finish rewrap and deprecate old KEK.
5) Recovery validation: Use snapshot manifest to replay key metadata in isolated sandbox and run crypto-checks (sign/verify, unwrap/rewrap) before returning to production.
6) Postmortem & Policy changes: Enforce ephemeral operator keys, tighten attestation cadence, and require periodic snapshot integrity checks.

Notes / design tradeoffs:
- We rely on an operator attestation service (remote cluster attestation) to avoid complete reliance on a single HSM. This requires us to ship an attestation agent in the Private control plane package.
- Snapshot encryption must be customer-KMS-bound (BYOK) so only the customer can decrypt; Redwood can store encrypted blobs but cannot decrypt without proper consent.
- Dual-wrap window reduces immediate outages but increases complexity; call it opt-in for high-availability customers.

I've attached a first-pass PDF + a short checklist that maps roles and expected commands. Please review for gaps (especially networking egress constraints and backup retention semantics for on-prem installs).

Thanks —
Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Key eviction & encrypted snapshot procedure for private deployments (KEP-SP)

Thanks for the write-up, Priyom. A few quick clarifying Qs from the ACME infra side: 

1) Snapshot destination: our compliance team requires that snapshots for DE & EU clusters do not cross region boundaries. Can the snapshot agent select bucket region per deployment?
2) How do you handle HSM attestation when the customer's HSM has intermittent connectivity to Redwood's attestation endpoint?
3) If we rotate the wrapping key, is there a safe rollback path in case the new wrapping key fails to decrypt an edge key?

We want to ensure DR tabletop exercises exercise both the dual-wrap window and a full rollback case. Happy to set up a short sync to walk through the checklist.

—ACME infra (infra-ops@acme.com)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: infra-ops@acme.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key eviction & encrypted snapshot procedure for private deployments (KEP-SP)

ACME — good questions, quick answers below and I expanded the checklist inside the PDF attachment: kep-sp-proposal-v1.pdf; also attached an operational checklist (kep-sp-checklist.xlsx) with Play IDs.

1) Region scoping: yes — snapshot agent will accept a deployment-level bucket ARN/URL and enforce region-scoped validation before upload. We will expose flags to deny cross-region replication and surface a hard validation error in the runbook.
2) Attestation: support a cached-attestation token mode — the attestation agent can present a signed time-limited token when connectivity is flaky; for elevated operations (eviction, rewrap) we require live attestation or multi-party signing (customer operator + Redwood validator). Documented in the checklist.
3) Rollback: we recommend keeping the previous wrapping key in a revoked-but-retained state for a 72-hour rollback TTL after rotation. The flow: if decrypt fails in the sandbox, re-enable the old wrapping key in read-only mode and use the snapshot manifest to rewrap; all actions logged and require 2-person approval. Full rollback is a deliberate, audited operation.

Operational asks for Redwood ops team:
- Ben, can you add the dual-wrap support to the rewrap API? Minimal surface: allow rewrap API to accept an array [old_key_id, new_key_id] with an optional ttl_seconds.
- Soojin, please confirm we can run the snapshot manifest replay as an isolated job in the Private control plane without exfiltrating keys to Redwood.
- Monica, let's schedule a 60-minute tabletop with ACME next week; propose Tue 2027-06-29 11:00 PT.

I'll push a v2 with edge-case flows later today.

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachment: kep-sp-checklist.xlsx (playbook matrix)

Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key eviction & encrypted snapshot procedure for private deployments (KEP-SP)

+1 on tabletop — Tue 06/29 11:00 PT works for me.

Ben: prioritize adding the dual-wrap parameter to the rewrap endpoint; scope it small (accept list, TTL) and gate behind a feature flag defaulted off. We want to test without shipping to hosted customers.

Soojin: confirm the sandbox replay pattern can be run fully on-prem under customer network policies (no outbound key material). We must be explicit in the runbook about required firewall rules and S3 endpoints.

Priyom — great first draft. Please call out operator revocation commands explicitly (two-liner sysadmin commands) in v2 so CS and our install engineers can run them during an incident. Also add a short decision tree at the top: "snapshot-first" vs "evict-first" depending on whether snapshot integrity can be confirmed.

I'll take the tabletop invite and loop in Solutions Engineering for scheduling.

—Monica
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
